title: Personalized rerank drift detection and NDCG/MRR A/B evaluation hooks
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement an end-to-end evaluation and monitoring pipeline for personalized reranking quality with NDCG/MRR tracking, integrated customer prompt-set sampling, and A/B test hooks. This ticket scopes the evaluation infra, drift detection heuristics, lightweight online instrumentation for A/B and canary runs, and the dashboarding/data retention plan. Goal: detect regressions in ranking quality per-customer segment while keeping telemetry cost and latency overhead within budget.
acceptance_criteria: NDCG@10 and MRR metrics emitted per experimental bucket and per-customer-segment to the metrics backend (prod and staging)
Sampling pipeline that ingests customer-provided promptsets and automatically maps them to segments; sampling rate configurable per-customer
A/B and canary hooks in the rerank endpoint that mark requests as part of an experiment and produce tagged telemetry (latency, token-cost, ndcg,mrr) at <= 2% additional per-request latency overhead
A drift detector that alerts when per-segment NDCG or embedding similarity distributions shift beyond threshold and creates a slack/ops incident with diagnostic artifacts
Dashboard (console) panels showing historical NDCG/MRR by model version and segment, and links to failed-examples export
End-to-end tests and a load test proving telemetry pipeline scales to expected Dedicated throughput (50k rerank calls/min) without dropped metrics
implementation_notes: Use offline eval worker to compute NDCG/MRR from logged candidate lists and relevance labels; prefer batched jobs to reduce cost

Online: instrument rerank API to emit compact evaluation events (request_id, model_version, bucket, candidate_order, topN_scores, elapsed_ms) to a streaming topic (kafka/ksql) for near-real-time aggregation
Customer promptset ingestion: provide S3/Drive ingest + UI mapping to customer_id -> segment; canonicalize tokenization to match production model tokenization
Drift detection: bootstrap with KS-test on embedding distributions and change-point detection on NDCG rolling windows (14d baseline). Alert thresholds are configurable by segment.
A/B hooks: lightweight flagging via experiment_id header. Ensure deterministic hashing to route repeated requests consistently for the same user/session
Telemetry budget: aim for telemetry event size < 2KB. If larger, fallback to sampling of candidate details to limit costs
Privacy: redact PII from logged prompts before storage; follow Private deployment KMS/HSM retention policy when requested by customer
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Full candidate logging enables accurate NDCG/MRR but increases storage/ingest costs. We will default to sampled full-logging for 5% of requests and compact summaries for the rest.
Real-time NDCG provides early detection but adds complexity; we will implement a hybrid: near-real-time aggregated metrics (1m windows) and offline full recomputation nightly.

Per-customer baselines improve sensitivity to regressions but require more historical storage. Start with per-segment baselines (tier/industry) and opt-in per-customer baselines for high-commit customers.
Embedding-based drift detection is cheaper than label-based but noisier. We'll combine both signals and require multiple triggers before firing a high-priority alert.

8) Performance validation and scale testing to target Dedicated load (owner: Perf Eng)
9) Documentation and runbook for incident response (owner: SRE)

risks: Telemetry cost growth if sampling/compaction is misconfigured
False positives from embedding drift detection leading to alert fatigue
Latency regressions at p99 if instrumentation allocates or blocks in hot path
Customer privacy concerns if prompt redaction misses sensitive tokens
